registryLegalName: Dismissal After Probation and Vacation of a Pre-1984 Conviction, RCW 9.95.240

config.documentTitleFull: MOTION AND APPLICATION TO VACATE THE RECORD OF CONVICTION PURSUANT TO RCW 9.95.240
config.courtCaption: IN THE SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Every defendant who has fulfilled the conditions of probation for the entire period, or who was discharged from probation before the period ended, may at any time before the maximum period of punishment for the offence expires be permitted in the court's discretion to withdraw a guilty plea and enter a plea of not guilty, or, where convicted after a plea of not guilty, have the verdict set aside. The court may then dismiss the information or indictment, after which the person is released from all penalties and disabilities resulting from the offence. A proviso preserves the conviction for pleading and proof in any subsequent prosecution for any other offence, with the same effect as if probation had not been granted.

After the period of probation has expired, the defendant may apply to the sentencing court for vacation of the record of conviction under RCW 9.94A.640, and the court may in its discretion clear the record if it finds the defendant has met the equivalent of the RCW 9.94A.640(2) tests as those tests would be applied to a person convicted of a crime committed before 1 July 1984.

Carries the clerk transmittal to the Washington State Patrol identification section and any local police agency, the immediate-update and FBI transmittal duties, and the bar on dissemination except to criminal justice enforcement agencies.
Supplies the tests applied on the subsection (2)(a) limb, as those tests would be applied to a person convicted of a crime committed before 1 July 1984.
Recognises RCW 9.95.240 as one of only four routes for removing a conviction from criminal history.

counselFlags: Pre-Sentencing Reform Act route only: the subsection (2)(a) limb applies the RCW 9.94A.640(2) tests as they would be applied to a person convicted of a crime committed before 1 July 1984. An offence committed on or after 1 July 1984 runs under RCW 9.94A.640 or RCW 9.96.060 directly, not under this section. Confirm the offence date before filing.

Two distinct limbs, two distinct timing rules. Subsection (1) has no waiting period but a deadline: the application must be made at any time before the maximum period of punishment for the offence expires, and it requires that the defendant fulfilled the conditions of probation for the entire period or was discharged early. Subsection (2)(a) runs the other way — it becomes available only after the period of probation has expired. Establish which limb applies before filing.

Relief is discretionary on both limbs. The court may permit withdrawal of the plea or set aside the verdict in its discretion, and may in its discretion clear the record. Nothing in this Motion asserts that the court has exercised or will exercise that discretion.

The conviction is preserved for later prosecutions. The subsection (1) proviso keeps the conviction available for pleading and proof in any subsequent prosecution for any other offence, with the same effect as if probation had not been granted. A participant must be told that this relief is not erasure.

Washington verification: RCW 9.95.240 prescribes no verification or notarization requirement and identifies no verification statute, and no pattern form supplies one. Confirm what the sentencing court's local rules require before signing; the source does not specify one.

Service requirements are not established. RCW 9.95.240 as read at source prescribes no service on the prosecuting attorney and no certificate of service, and no pattern form supplies one. No certificate of service is drafted; confirm local rules with the clerk before filing.
Filing fee: the source does not establish a filing fee for a vacation petition in district, municipal or superior court. No amount may be stated to a participant; confirm with the clerk.

Local requirements vary: the Washington Courts local-rule warning means some counties impose additional local requirements. Which counties, and what they require, was not established at source, so the packet carries a local-check instruction instead.

On vacation the clerk transmits to the Washington State Patrol identification section and any local police agency, with immediate-update and FBI transmittal duties, and dissemination is barred except to criminal justice enforcement agencies. Those are the clerk's and agencies' duties, not the participant's, and this Motion never asserts that they have been performed.

No pattern form exists for RCW 9.95.240 and the section prescribes none, so this pleading is drafted on the RCW 9.94A.640 model. If Washington later publishes a pattern form for this section, this instrument must be revisited.

waitingPeriods.duration: None, but there is a deadline instead: the application must be made at any time before the maximum period of punishment for the offence expires.
After the period of probation has expired, and then the equivalent of the RCW 9.94A.640(2) tests as applied to a pre-1 July 1984 offence.

exclusions: On the subsection (1) limb, any application made after the maximum period of punishment for the offence has expired.
On the subsection (1) limb, any defendant who did not fulfil the conditions of probation for the entire period and was not discharged early.
On the subsection (2)(a) limb, any offence committed on or after 1 July 1984, for which RCW 9.94A.640 or RCW 9.96.060 applies directly.
Any expectation that the conviction disappears for later prosecutions: the subsection (1) proviso preserves it for pleading and proof in any subsequent prosecution for any other offence.
